concepts.title: Day arc
concepts.rationale: The sun mid-morning on its arc above a horizon, held in a cell. It is the brand idea in one mark and it can be animated: the sun moves.

concepts.title: Stored layers
concepts.rationale: Three layers for store, use and reserve. Clear as a battery metaphor, but generic: it could belong to any storage product.

concepts.title: H field
concepts.rationale: The initial cut from a solid disc. Strong at small sizes, but says nothing about energy or time.

selectionReason: Only the day arc carries the direction's signature, and it is the one concept that every other deliverable can echo: scroll story, chart, app dial and the light on the product.
headline: Your home's energy, from sunrise to night

strategy.differentiation: The category speaks either like industrial equipment or like a gadget. Haldora speaks like a household: it describes energy as a day and uses warm, editorial design where competitors use dark dashboards or white gloss.
territories: Quiet Current (rejected: gadget minimalism, needs renders the client lacks)
competitorNotes: Competitor descriptions are category conventions taken from the brief; no competitor audit was performed for this demonstration.

signature.name: The day arc
rules: Construction: the horizon sits at 66% of the format's height; the arc is half an ellipse standing on it, 40% of the width in radius and 50% of the height tall.
The sun travels the arc from left (sunrise) to right (sunset). This direction never mirrors, in Arabic or any other language: it depicts the sky, not reading order.
One sun per composition. If a picture already contains a sun, nothing else may draw one over it.
The arc is dashed in illustration, interface and motion (dash one unit, gap about three). It is solid only in the logo symbol, where dashes would fill in at small sizes.
The sun is brand amber in daylight and pale parchment against dawn, dusk and night skies, where amber would disappear.
At night there is no sun above the horizon: it is replaced by a smaller pale crescent, or left out.
Headline text has right of way: the arc stops at the edges of a text block and stars are kept out of it.
dont: Do not draw two arcs or two suns in one picture.
Do not mirror the arc for right-to-left layouts.
Do not run the arc through a headline.
Do not use the arc as a generic rainbow or a progress bar.

arabic.headline: طاقة بيتك، من شروق الشمس إلى الليل
arabic.body: حين ينتج السطح أكثر من حاجة البيت تحتفظ البطارية بالفائض، وتعيده إليك في ساعات المساء المزدحمة.
arabic.label: في البطارية
rules: Arabic is set in IBM Plex Sans Arabic throughout. It does not imitate the Latin serif and sans pairing; weight and measure carry the hierarchy instead.

Headlines: weight 700, line height 1.25, tracking 0. Statements and quotations: weight 600, one size above body, line height 1.7. Body: weight 400, line height 1.75. Labels: weight 600 at the small size.
Never set Arabic words in the monospaced face. It is for figures and units only, which stay in Latin digits and read left to right inside right-to-left text.
Arabic text is never letter-spaced and never set in capitals-style small sizes below 14px.
arabic.lockupRule: The logo is the Latin wordmark in every market; there is no Arabic lockup. In Arabic layouts the lockup sits at the reading (right) edge, and the name may be written out in Arabic in running text as هالدورا.
